379YE Autumn Equinox Announcements by th.d: Palladius of Urizen commissioned further research through the civil service into the Skarsind Runeforge, following a suggestion by Peter of Hintown. The Minister for Historical Research approved the action, and 5 thrones were provided after the Autumn Equinox 379YE to fund it. As a result, a small expedition was sent to western Sermersuaq to investigate sites there that bear on Peter of Hintown's theory directly. The page records the dispatch of this expedition but gives no findings.

n.Imperial Orcs: The research concerns the Runeforge in Skarsind, a territory the Imperial Orcs held at the time, though the page says nothing of the orcs themselves.
n.Urizen: Palladius of Urizen commissioned the follow-up research, which led to an expedition being sent to western Sermersuaq.
n.Wintermark: An Imperial research expedition was sent into western Sermersuaq, Wintermark's territory, to investigate sites linked to Peter of Hintown's theory about the Runeforge.

t.Sermersuaq: A small expedition was dispatched to western Sermersuaq to investigate sites there relevant to Peter of Hintown's theory about the Skarsind Runeforge.
t.Skarsind: The Skarsind Runeforge is the subject of the commissioned research, though the expedition itself went to Sermersuaq rather than Skarsind.

379YE Autumn Equinox Imperial elections.d: New senators took the seats for Kahraman, Semmerholm, Upwold and Volodmartz. Incumbents held Casinea, Tassato, Therunin, Morrow and Hahnmark. Skarsind's seat was left vacant after the ratification of Relinquish Skarsind. The titles of Minister of Historical Research and Imperial Master of Works lapsed, and other Imperial titles went to new holders. Six generals were appointed, four of them incumbents. The Synod named Cardinals and Gatekeepers of Loyalty and Pride and several Virtue Inquisitors, though the Inquisitor of Prosperity post stayed vacant. Bourse seats were awarded for up to 500 Thrones. The Legacy remains held by the Grendel and must be allocated once Spiral is again Imperial.

n.Dawn: Dawn did well in the Synod, winning the Cardinal of Pride (Ozren de Orzel), the Gatekeeper of Pride (Lady Josephine Novarion) and the Virtue Inquisitor of Courage (Lady Eleanor de Rondell). Bohemond de Rondell became Senator for Semmerholm.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are noted as holding the Legacy, which will need allocating when Spiral is once again Imperial.
n.Highguard: Jared of the Suns of Courous of Highguard became Cardinal of Loyalty and Ephreal became Virtue Inquisitor of Pride. Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold kept Casinea's Senate seat.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs lost their Senate seat for Skarsind, which was left vacant after Relinquish Skarsind was ratified.
n.Navarr: Navarr kept its voice for Therunin, with Caerwyn Summer Crow returned as incumbent senator.
n.The Brass Coast: Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza became Senator for Kahraman. Joaquim i Shartha i Riqueza was named Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills.
n.The League: The League kept Tassato's Senate seat through Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato. Its citizens also won four Virtue Inquisitor posts: Ambition, Loyalty, Vigilance and Wisdom.
n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new Senator for Upwold, Silas.
n.Urizen: Ariadne was returned as Senator for Morrow. Anna-Valeria Cascade of Urizen became Gatekeeper of Loyalty.
n.Varushka: Juha the Cave Spider became Senator for Volodmartz. Simargl, the Empty One, of the Circle of Zulgan-Tash of Varushka became Dean of the Lyceum.
n.Wintermark: Hengest Dun kept Hahnmark's Senate seat, and Yarrick Ursan of Wintermark became Virtue Inquisitor of The Way.

t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun was re-elected as Senator for Hahnmark.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman gained a new senator, Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza.
t.Morrow: Ariadne was re-elected as Senator for Morrow.

t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato was re-elected as Senator for Tassato.
t.Therunin: Caerwyn Summer Crow was re-elected as Senator for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Upwold gained a new senator, Silas.
t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz gained a new senator, Juha the Cave Spider.

379YE Autumn Equinox winds of fortune.d: This summary page linked to many separate events. The vyig suffered setbacks in Sarvos. A briar demagogue spread lies in the Marches. Varushkans in Karsk sought closer ties with their cousins. The Fellowship of Purple Sails took a renewed interest in politics. Fog descended on the Bay of Catazar, and an ancient runeforge was found in Gildenheim. Salt Lord Suriad of the Grendel wrote to the Empire. There was talk of reviving the Hearth Tithe. Skarsind's miners grew restless and a curse struck Urizen. The herald Reed sought a Declaration of Amity. The Castle of Thorns appeared to be failing, vallorn transformations spread from Brocéliande, orcs entered Segura and Jotun raids were repelled. The Reikos flux continued, and exorcisms were ordered at Ennerlund and Reikos.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Castle of Thorns in Astolat, the old seat of its monarchs, appeared to be falling down, and vallorn transformations spilled into Astolat and Semmerholm. Ozren de Orzel of Dawn had been named to oversee the exorcism of the Great Pits at Ennerlund.
n.Druj: The Reikos flux cut a swathe through the Imperial armies fighting the Druj at Urith Barath, in a territory the Druj held.
n.Grendel: The Grendel Salt Lord Suriad sent a reasonably open letter to the Empire about recent treaty negotiations.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Casinea suffered odd transformations from vallorn activity spilling over from Brocéliande, and Highborn benefactors were among the backers of the Fellowship of Purple Sails.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind was due to be handed over to the Imperial Orcs, prompting miners to strip it of metal and spreading dissatisfaction. The presence of Imperial Orc companies in Reikos showed that the flux appears to affect only humans.
n.Jotun: Jotun raids in the west of the Empire were decisively driven back by fortifications and Imperial armies, as the conflict with the Empire moved into an active phase.
n.The Brass Coast: A significant force of orcs crossed from the Lasambrian hills into Segura, and supernatural fog descended along the southern Imperial coast.
n.The League: The vyig suffered significant setbacks in Sarvos, opening an opportunity to dislodge them from the League's cities, while an exorcism of the Great Pits at Ennerlund in Holberg was under way.
n.Urizen: A powerful curse struck the mountains of Urizen, halving crystal mana from its mana sites and causing more than one catastrophic loss of poise.
n.Varushka: With hostilities in Karsk at an end, the Varushkan inhabitants of its northern vales were seeking closer ties with their estranged cousins.
n.Wintermark: With the Jotun conflict turning active, there was talk in Wintermark and the Marches of reviving the Hearth Tithe.

t.Astolat: Unsettling events struck the Castle of Thorns, the Empire's première academy for civil servants, which appeared to be falling down, and vallorn-driven transformations spilled into the territory.
t.Bay of Catazar: A bank of supernatural fog descended and seemed to stretch along the entire northern half of the bay.
t.Brocéliande: Vallorn activity along Brocéliande's borders spilled over into neighbouring territories, leaving a wave of odd transformations.
t.Casinea: Vallorn activity from Brocéliande spilled into Casinea, leaving odd transformations in its wake.
t.Holberg: The exorcism of the haunted Great Pits at Ennerlund continued under Ozren de Orzel, appointed by the Synod.
t.Karsk: Following the cessation of hostilities, the Varushkan inhabitants of Karsk's northern vales sought closer ties with their estranged cousins.
t.Reikos: The flux continued to rage, damaging resources and ravaging the armies at Urith Barath, while the Synod named High Exorcist Solas to cleanse the haunted Vigilant Swan.
t.Sarvos: The vyig suffered significant setbacks, creating an opportunity to finally dislodge them from the city.
t.Segura: A significant force of orcs crossed into Segura from the Lasambrian hills.
t.Semmerholm: Vallorn activity spilling over from Brocéliande left odd transformations across Semmerholm.
t.Skarsind: Ahead of the handover to the Imperial Orcs, miners were urged to extract as much metal as they could, and dissatisfaction spread.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits at Ennerlund, haunted since the previous season, were being exorcised under the oversight of Ozren de Orzel of Dawn.

379YE Autumn Equinox winds of war.d: The Thule left Crowslook and Branoc, which are now neutral, and occupied the Silver Peaks and Stonefield Ice Caves. The Black Thorns cut through Brocéliande and retook Elerael. The Barrens orcs made a confused attack on Drycastle and the Towers of the Dawn, then withdrew. In Holberg, animated trees battered the defences. The Granite Pillar and Quiet Step slowed but could not stop the Grendel in Ateri. In Reikos, Haros Water was cleared, but around 3,500 Imperial troops were lost at Urith Barath to battle and the Reikos flux, and the Winter-animated husks rotted away. Thirty Imperial captains could not stop the Jotun routing the Hierro. The Grendel left Feroz for Kalino.

n.Dawn: Dawnish defenders at Drycastle and the Towers of the Dawn rebuffed a half-hearted Barrens orc attack, and House de Cassilon hosted the Golden Sun at Spiral Castle after ending their decade behind the mists.
n.Druj: The Stone Toad were driven out of Haros Water but held Urith Barath against five Imperial armies, untouched by the flux, while scattered Druj remnants in Holberg turned to banditry.
n.Grendel: The Salt Lords won the first stage of the Siege of Fort Mezudan and took nearly half of Ateri, while their navy left Feroz and appears to have landed a major force in Kalino.
n.Highguard: The Granite Pillar led the defence of Fort Mezudan and bore the bulk of the damage, while the Valiant Pegasus led the costly assault on Urith Barath and fell first and worst to the Reikos flux.
n.Jotun: Jotun armies routed the Lasambrians and took more than half of Reinos, but their raiders on the Wintermark border were savagely beaten back, and they have sent no word to the Empire since warning against aiding the Lasambrians.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns took losses forcing their way through the vallorn to reclaim Elerael, and Navarr scouts with the Quiet Step supported the defence of Fort Mezudan.
n.The Brass Coast: Imperial armies sent to Feroz found the Grendel gone and spent a peaceful season there, and Suranni merchants on the Brass Coast brought news of the fighting in Kalino.
n.The League: The Wolves of War and their Varushkan wagon-raiders joined the bloody siege of Urith Barath, while League-held Holberg was beset by animated trees.
n.Thule: Under the peace treaty the Thule left Crowslook and Branoc to expand their camp in Krevsaty, and took the Silver Peaks and the ilium-rich Stonefield Ice Caves unopposed.
n.Urizen: The Urizen garrison at Fort Mezudan, their last foothold in Spiral, was besieged by the Grendel, and an Urizen army took heavy losses to disease before Urith Barath.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe held Karsk in uneasy peace, the Charnel Lord's forces kept to the Broken Barrow, and Varushkans made up much of the Imperial force in the Lasambrian Hills and the Wolves of War's mercenaries.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's armies left the Silver Peaks to the Thule while the Green Shield guarded the plains, and they vented their frustration by nearly routing Jotun raiders, as many Wintermark captains fought in Reinos.

t.Brocéliande: The Black Thorns pushed past the vallorn to drive insect abominations and Druj bands out of the southern forests, returning Elerael to Imperial hands.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Fraser de Cassilon names it among the far places of the Empire he longs to see.
t.Feroz: The Grendel fleet had sailed south before the Imperial armies arrived, so the Seventh Wave, the Tusks and the Fire of the South spent a peaceful late Summer there.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: an Imperial orc legionnaire tells stories of a battle with the Thule there.
t.Holberg: Old Tom's Finest spent the Summer fighting animated trees left by Druj magic, while remnant Druj bands in the northern forests turned to brigandage.
t.Kalino: The Naguerro broke with their allies to defend Kalino and appear to be stalling a much larger Iron Confederacy army, even as a major Grendel force landed on the eastern coast.
t.Karsk: With peace, the Thule left Crowslook and Branoc as neutral ground and dug in at Krevsaty, while the Golden Axe held a wary defence and the Charnel Lord's forces waited at the Broken Barrow.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar and the Quiet Step marched through its mountains on their way to Spiral.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar and the Quiet Step marched through its mountains on their way to Spiral.
t.Reikos: Five Imperial armies cleared Haros Water, so two regions are now Imperial, but lost thousands to battle and the Reikos flux besieging Urith Barath on the site of High Chalcis.
t.Reinos: The Jotun outnumbered the Lasambrians four to one and, despite some three thousand Imperial soldiers fighting with the Hierro, routed them and took more than half the territory.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: the Hierro chieftain is credited with forging the Lasambrian alliance that conquered Segura.
t.Sermersuaq: Imperial forces withdrew under the treaty and the Thule took the Silver Peaks and Stonefield Ice Caves without a fight, leaving an uneasy peace.
t.Spiral: The Grendel besieged Fort Mezudan, the last Urizen holding here, and now control nearly half of Ateri.
t.The Barrens: The Black Thorns crossed the Barrens with the help of the Orcs of the Great Forest, after which up to fifteen thousand Barrens orcs made a confused, failed attempt on Drycastle and the Towers of the Dawn.
t.The Semmerlak: The Golden Axe camped near the remains of Ivarsgard on its shores, now being reclaimed by forest, and cleared wolves from the ruins and old mines.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Fraser de Cassilon names it among the far places of the Empire he longs to see.
t.Weirwater: The Golden Sun were lavishly hosted and resupplied by House de Cassilon at Spiral Castle, which is to receive its first new Castellan in over a decade.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr who stayed behind there received word that the Black Thorns had reached Elerael.
r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: The Black Thorns skirted these vallorn-held woods at speed but still lost soldiers to husks, ettercaps and stranger horrors.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: The Black Thorns drove out insect abominations and Druj bands so that the miasma receded, putting the region back in Imperial hands, though the army is now hemmed in by dangers on every side.
r.Holberg/Holfried: Marcher yeomen bought nearly every axe in Holfried's markets to fight the animated trees attacking Holberg's walls.
r.Karsk/Branoc: The Thule quietly left the hills of Branoc, leaving the region neutral and open to an Imperial army to claim, perhaps without resistance.
r.Karsk/Crowslook: The Thule quietly left the hills of Crowslook, leaving the region neutral and open to an Imperial army to claim, perhaps without resistance.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The withdrawing Thule massed here and greatly expanded their camp at the ruins of Oloy, to the alarm of the isolated defenders of the Krevsaty Yelta.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: Mentioned in passing: its miners profited from the Golden Axe's repairs and re-equipping.
r.Reikos/Haros Water: The last major Druj enclaves were rooted out of Haros Water, where the Valiant Pegasus had sheltered in the ruins of Haros, and the region is now in Imperial hands.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Green Shield watched from its open plains, ready to stop any Thule advance beyond the foothills, though none came.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The region was surrendered to the Thule, whose white dire-wolf banner now flies there and who expect an excellent bladeroot harvest from the fallen.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The Green Shield watched from its open plains, ready to stop any Thule advance beyond the foothills, though none came.
r.Spiral/Ateri: The Grendel overran the foothills and several spires and began the Siege of Fort Mezudan, which still stands but has been badly damaged.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: The Black Thorns set out through Dawnguard, after which the Barrens orcs launched sporadic attacks on Drycastle and the Towers of the Dawn, expecting a surrender that never came.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: The Black Thorns passed safely through Murderdale with the aid of the Orcs of the Great Forest on their way into Brocéliande.

A big sleep.d: Interrogations after the Summer Solstice raid led to warrants against lower-tier vyig agents and sympathisers, and within weeks vyig operations in Sarvos, along with other criminal enterprises, were shut down. Militia recruitment surged as fear of the vyig waned. Only Livueta Garovich di Sarvos, a brutal lieutenant of "Uncle Sarvos", escaped and remains wanted. Seized assets, two businesses, a farm and a forest, were offered to League citizens. The Vigilance assembly then named Vladimir von Temeschwar (Holberg), Valimir von Temeschwar (Tassato) and Irada von Temeschwar (Temeschwar) to lead campaigns funded with liao. All three chose active opposition, which significantly damages the vyig but cuts business production in those cities by a quarter.

n.The League: League heroes and magistrates broke the vyig in Sarvos and launched a campaign against them in the other three cities, though at the cost of disrupted trade in Holberg, Tassato and Temeschwar.

t.Holberg: Vladimir von Temeschwar of the Brotherhood of the Ashen Tower was appointed to lead active opposition to the vyig in the city, significantly damaging vyig activity while cutting all business production there by a quarter.
t.Sarvos: Vyig operations in the Jewelled City were brought to a close, militia enthusiasm surged, and seized vyig assets were put up for auction. Livueta Garovich di Sarvos remains at large under an outstanding warrant.
t.Tassato: Valimir von Temeschwar of the Red Tower was appointed to lead active opposition to the vyig in Tassato, significantly damaging vyig activity but disrupting business production there by a quarter.
t.Temeschwar: Irada von Temeschwar was appointed to lead active opposition to the vyig in Temeschwar, where the vyig were expected to be hardest to dislodge, and businesses there lost a quarter of their production through the disruption.

Appoint Sumaah ambassador.d: The motion was raised at the last Senate session of the Autumn Equinox summit. Under the Senate's rules for elections, the vote was therefore held at the first session of the Winter Solstice 379YE. No candidate received enough support, and the title of Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic remained unfilled. With the Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis completed, the Senate was expected to have another opportunity to appoint an ambassador in Spring 380YE.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named, but the Sumaah Embassy that offers the next chance to fill the post stands in Necropolis, a Highguard territory.

t.Necropolis: The completed Sumaah Embassy in Necropolis was expected to give the Senate a fresh opportunity to appoint an ambassador in Spring 380YE.

Appoint Throne IV.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Therunin, the motion sought to elect an Imperial Citizen to the Throne. Three nominees stood: Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, Senator for Sermersuaq; General Vanhe Korppi of the Fist of the Mountain; and Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, the Conscience of the Senate. The campaign ended without a result because no single candidate gained sufficient votes, so the Throne remained unfilled after this attempt.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Senator for Sermersuaq, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, stood for the Throne but did not win enough votes to be elected.

t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: the territory's senator, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason, was one of the three nominees for the Throne.

Archive:379YE Autumn Equinox Imperial ti.d: The roster named the senators for each territory, the generals of every Imperial army, the cardinals, gatekeepers and virtue inquisitors of the Synod, the Conclave's archmagi and grandmasters, and the holders of Imperial, national and minor Bourse positions. Several posts stood vacant, including the Imperial Master of Works, the Minister of Historical Research, the Admiral and the Virtue Inquisitor of Prosperity. The Great Forest at Reikos and the Vigilant Swan were back under Imperial control and awaited Senate allocation. The Great Pits of Ennerlund were being repaired and could be allocated now that Holberg was Imperial again. The Legacy remained in Grendel hands until Spiral was retaken.

n.Dawn: Dawn held the Senate seats of Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater and fielded three generals: Tancred de Rondell, Starac Sijed Orzel and Richard Vandale. Its nobles also held the cardinalships of Pride and Wisdom and the Archmage of Autumn's seat through Maurice de Gauvain.
n.Grendel: The Grendel held Spiral and with it the Bourse seat of the Legacy, which could not be allocated until the territory was Imperial once more.
n.Highguard: Highguard's senators Solomon, Zephram and Adamah sat for Bastion, Casinea and Necropolis. Generals Cuth, Mathayus and Jericho led its armies, and Highborn held the cardinalships of Courage, Loyalty and Vigilance as well as the post of Imperial Magus.
n.Imperial Orcs: Morgur Bloodcrow commanded the Winter Sun and Irontide Skar the Summer Storm, while Irontide Kul held the national Bourse seat of the Steel Fist.
n.Navarr: Navarr's senators were Rhain, Llewellyn Leafstalker and Caerwyn Summer Crow, and its generals were Carr Foxden of the Black Thorns and Merryn Farkas of the Quiet Step. Hywel Summercrow served as Chaplain Consular and Idris Eternal held the Thimble.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn held four Senate seats and fielded two generals, Estana i Mestiere i Guerra of the Red Wind Corsairs and Elias i Lemora i Erigo of the Fire of the South. They also held the Broken Shore Bounty and several sinecures and minor Bourse titles.
n.The League: The League sat four senators, including Rossalyn Jordan for a newly restored Holberg, and General Gabriel Barossa led the Wolves of War. Leaguers held the Conscience of the Senate, the Imperial Inquisitor's post, the Ambition cardinalship and the Master of the Imperial Mint.
n.The Marches: The Marches sat senators Orrick, Bridget Eastville and Silas and fielded four generals: Nedry, Richard Talbot, Jack Flint and Alusair Farstrider. Silent John was Gatekeeper of Ambition and Robert Shanks operated Brock's Toll.
n.Urizen: Urizen's senators were Ariadne, Probus and Cato, and General Nicassia Avicia led the Citadel Guard. Urizeni also held the post of High Exorcist and the gatekeeperships of Loyalty and Wisdom.
n.Varushka: Varushka sat four senators and fielded generals Valentin Brossa of the Northern Eagle and Magnus Anatolyvich Prochnost of the Golden Axe. Its people also held the Eternal Shafts of Time, the Granites of Veltsgorsk and the post of Dean of the Lyceum.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senators sat for Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, and Generals Marius Fjellrevening and Vanhe Korppi led its armies. Its people also held the cardinalships of Prosperity and the Way, the post of Imperial Consul and two national Bourse seats.

Archive:379YE Winter Solstice Imperial t.d: The record named the senator for each Imperial territory and the generals of each nation's armies. It also listed Senate appointments and sinecures, the cardinals, gatekeepers and inquisitors of the Synod, the archmagi and grandmasters of the Conclave, and Bourse seats with their bids. Several posts stood vacant, including the Imperial Master of Works, the Admiral and the Wisdom Gatekeeper. Senator Dušan of Miekarova had been revoked by the Synod but was re-elected. The Great Forest at Reikos had returned to Imperial control and awaited Senate allocation. The Legacy was held by the Grendel, and the Great Pits of Ennerlund were being repaired.

n.Dawn: Dawn's senators were Bohemond de Rondell, Escaladus DeCarsenere and Valentin Ivarovich Orzel, and its generals led the Hounds of Glory, Golden Sun and Eastern Sky; Dawn also held the Pride and Wisdom cardinalships.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named, but Reikos had a Highguard senator listed and the Great Forest at Reikos was recorded as back within Imperial control.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel held the Legacy, which would need allocating once Spiral was again an Imperial territory.
n.Highguard: Highguard had four senators, including Gideon for Reikos, and generals for the Seventh Wave, Granite Pillar and Valiant Pegasus. It held the Courage, Loyalty and Vigilance cardinalships, and Asael held the Vigilant Swan.
n.Imperial Orcs: Irontide Vio sat as senator for Skarsind, Morgur Bloodcrow and Irontide Skar led the Winter Sun and Summer Storm, and Irontide Kul held the Steel Fist.

n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn had four senators and fielded the Red Wind Corsairs, the Fire of the South and the Freeborn Storm fleet. Karlos i Shartha i Riqueza held the Broken Shore Bounty.
n.The League: The League had four senators, and Gabriel Barossa and Andrea von Holberg led its two armies. Leaguers held the Ambition cardinalship, the post of Imperial Inquisitor and the Master of the Imperial Mint.
n.The Marches: The Marches had senators for Bregasland, Mitwold and Upwold and four generals, including those of the Drakes and the Strong Reeds. Silent John was Ambition Gatekeeper and Robert Shanks operated Brock's Toll.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule were listed as holding Wintermark's Stonefield Ice Caves.
n.Urizen: Urizen had senators for Morrow, Redoubt and Zenith, and its single general, Nicassia Avicia, led the Citadel Guard; Solas of Urizen was High Exorcist.
n.Varushka: Varushka had four senators, including Dušan, who was re-elected after Synod revocation. Its generals led the Northern Eagle and Golden Axe, and Varushkans held the Eternal Shafts of Time and the Granites of Veltsgorsk.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark had senators for Hahnmark, Kallavesa and Sermersuaq, and generals Volk and Horsa Tyrshalt. Kellua Itsepainen was Imperial Consul, but its Stonefield Ice Caves were held by the Thule.

t.Astolat: Bohemond de Rondell was recorded as senator for Astolat.
t.Bastion: Solomon of the Shattered Tower was recorded as senator for Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Orrick was recorded as senator for Bregasland, the Dour Fens.
t.Casinea: Zephram of Cantiarch's Hold was recorded as senator for Casinea.
t.Feroz: Liythos i Purjo i Guerra was recorded as senator for Feroz.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun was recorded as senator for Hahnmark.
t.Hercynia: Ranulf Pridestalker was recorded as senator for Hercynia.
t.Holberg: Rossalyn Jordan was senator for Holberg, and the Great Pits of Ennerlund within it were under repair.
t.Kahraman: Maher i Zaydan i Riqueza was recorded as senator for Kahraman.
t.Kallavesa: Olle Markusson was recorded as senator for Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Maximov Strascovich was recorded as senator for Karov.
t.Karsk: Radomir was recorded as senator for Karsk.
t.Madruga: Anwar i Del-Toro i Riqueza was recorded as senator for Madruga.
t.Miaren: Llewellyn Leafstalker was recorded as senator for Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Dušan Otecovna Zlata was senator for Miekarova; he had been revoked by the Synod but re-elected, and could not be revoked again until after the next normal election.
t.Mitwold: Bridget Eastville was recorded as senator for Mitwold, Pride of the Marches.
t.Morrow: Ariadne was recorded as senator for Morrow.
t.Necropolis: Ianthe of Raven's Watch was recorded as senator for Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Probus of Shattered Spire was recorded as senator for Redoubt.
t.Reikos: Gideon of the Suns of Couros was listed as senator for Reikos. The Great Forest at Reikos was back within Imperial control and ready for the Senate to allocate.
t.Sarvos: Mirislav was recorded as senator for Sarvos.
t.Segura: Avisena i Ezmara i Guerra was recorded as senator for Segura.
t.Semmerholm: Escaladus DeCarsenere was recorded as senator for Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte was recorded as senator for Sermersuaq.
t.Skarsind: Irontide Vio was recorded as senator for Skarsind.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: no senator was listed for Spiral. The Legacy was to be allocated once Spiral was again an Imperial territory, and Damian was named Castellan of Spiral Castle.
t.Tassato: Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato was recorded as senator for Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Gant Archama was recorded as senator for Temeschwar.
t.Therunin: Caerwyn Summer Crow was recorded as senator for Therunin.
t.Upwold: Silas was recorded as senator for Upwold, the Silver Chase.
t.Volodmartz: Juha the Cave Spider was recorded as senator for Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Valentin Ivarovich Orzel was senator for Weirwater, and the Weirwater Vales Bourse seat was held by Soren il Signo for 400 Thrones.
t.Zenith: Tanwyn Ankarien was recorded as senator for Zenith.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: The Great Pits of Ennerlund were being repaired and were expected to produce their first mithril shortly after the Summer Solstice 380YE.

Assignment of Skarsind II.d: The motion allocated Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs, making it their territory and entitling it to elect a Senator. Skarsind ceased to be a Wintermark territory, with significant implications for any Winterfolk still living there. Constitutionally, a method was settled by which the Imperial Orcs appoint a senator, and this directly affected how they appoint their Generals and similar titles.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gained Skarsind as their own territory and the right to a Senator, and the method settled for that appointment reshaped how they choose their Generals and similar titles.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark lost Skarsind as one of its territories, with significant implications for any Winterfolk still living there.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind passed from Wintermark to the Imperial Orcs and could now elect a Senator to represent it.

Briar liar.d: Tobin, accompanied by his sister, told crowds that the Carstokes had tried to murder him for being a Briar, displaying his Briar patches as proof. Margary Bolholt of the militia exposed him: he had blamed the Trammels at Tower March, the Bolholts elsewhere and, by a report from Anvil, the Talbots. She arrested him and his sister on suspicion of stealing a Carstoke sheep. In the chaos that followed, accounts differed over who drew a knife, but Margary was stabbed twice and killed, and the siblings fled. Magistrates asked law-abiding citizens to watch for the suspect. His rhetoric urging Briars to stand together against an oppressive system has found some acceptance, and the longer he remains free, the more dangerous he may become.

n.The Marches: A Briar demagogue is stoking resentment between Briars and the Marcher establishment with lies against families such as the Carstokes, Trammels, Bolholts and Talbots, and he killed or fled the killing of a young Bolholt militia member. He remains a small but growing threat to the nation's stability.

t.Upwold: Upwold saw the firebrand stir crowds in several places and the death of militia member Margary Bolholt, and its magistrates are now asking citizens to report sightings of the fugitive.

r.Upwold/Birchland: Tobin was tracked to Birchland and confronted before a crowd. Young Margary Bolholt was stabbed to death there, and he and his sister fled.
r.Upwold/Tower March: Mentioned in passing: Tobin had earlier appeared at Tower March, claiming there that the Trammels had beaten him.

Construct Reckoners Reward.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Karov, the motion commissioned a sinecure in Sarvos costing 12 wains of mithril and 3 Thrones of labour. It passed at 10 Thrones, which were disbursed to Senator Tassato. The holder, The Book Keeper, was to be appointed by unanimous decision of the League senators, and completion would automatically create this League national Imperial title. No location within Sarvos was specified, leaving the choice to the senator. No progress was recorded at the Autumn Equinox 379YE, and by the Autumn Equinox 380YE the commission had lapsed without being built.

n.The League: The League stood to gain a new national title, The Book Keeper, appointed unanimously by its senators and drawing mana crystals from the sinecure, but the commission lapsed before completion and the title was never created.

t.Sarvos: Reckoners Reward was to be built somewhere in Sarvos at the senator's discretion, but no work was recorded and the commission lapsed by Autumn 380YE.

Construct the Hearth of the Tempest.d: Proposed by the senator for Miekarova and seconded by Volodmartz, the motion called for a folly in Mieriada to be handed into the control of the Spring Eternal Papa Otec, who would operate it as a College of Magic specialising in the Spring realm without ongoing cost to the Senate. After the Autumn Equinox 379YE, Dušan Otecovna Zlata supplied the materials and money: one wain of white granite, one wain of weirwood and four crowns. The official Imperial work was completed. During the Spring Equinox 380YE the folly underwent a dramatic transformation into the Heart of the Tempest.

n.Varushka: Varushkan senators for Miekarova and Volodmartz brought the motion, and the Varushkan Dušan Otecovna Zlata funded it, placing a Spring college under Papa Otec in Varushkan lands.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova gained the Hearth of the Tempest, a folly given to Papa Otec to serve as a college of Spring magic, which later transformed into the Heart of the Tempest.

r.Miekarova/Mieriada: Mieriada became the site of the Hearth of the Tempest, a folly in Papa Otec's control that transformed into the Heart of the Tempest at the Spring Equinox 380YE.

Crow on the cradle.d: Since the Thule invasion of 368YE, a force of Varushkans, Wolves and orc bandits loyal to the Charnel Lord fought from the Broken Hill, eventually backing the Varushkan defenders. As the Thule pulled back to Krevsaty, the Charnel Lord called on old oaths sworn by the Malinov, Sloev and Pravin of Moresvah, who once led the Iron Helm before Empress Mariika disbanded it. His warriors could enlarge an existing army or form the core of a reborn Iron Helm. Years of war had ruined Karsk's roads, so Varushka could not support a third army without repairs. The Senate agreed to rebuild the roads, which was finished shortly before the Spring Equinox 380YE, and to restore the Iron Helm.

n.Thule: The Thule had made at least a short-term peace and withdrawn from Branoc and Crowslook to Krevsaty, though the Charnel Lord predicted that the peace would not last.
n.Varushka: Varushka was offered the Charnel Lord's warriors and the help of the old Moresvah families. The Senate chose to rebuild Karsk's roads so that a third army could be supported and to restore the Iron Helm under the black banner.

t.Karsk: War had left Karsk's road network ruined. The great work to rebuild it was completed before the Spring Equinox 380YE, allowing a third Varushkan army to be supported and permanently boosting the territory's mines and forests.

r.Karsk/Branoc: The Thule withdrew from Branoc, and the Charnel Lord prepared to sleep in the Broken Hill, leaving Baruk and his blood-kin to guard the barrow. Some vales here supplied the warriors offered to Varushka.
r.Karsk/Crowslook: The Thule withdrew from Crowslook, whose vales included followers of the Charnel Lord available to join a Varushkan army.
r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Krevsaty was where the Thule withdrew to after leaving Branoc and Crowslook.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The Malinov, Sloev and Pravin families of Moresvah were reminded of their oath to raise the Iron Helm's black banner again, and the Moresvah miners were key to restoring that army.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: Mentioned in passing: vales in eastern Nitrost were among those whose people followed the Charnel Lord.

Disburse funds for The Towerjacks.d: Proposed by Holberg and seconded by Sarvos, the motion requested additional Senate funds towards the commission of The Towerjacks, an army of the League. It passed in principle at a sum of 350 thrones, and that amount was disbursed to Senator Holberg to continue the construction work.

n.The League: The League's planned new army, The Towerjacks, received 350 thrones of Senate funding towards its continued construction.

t.Holberg: Holberg's senator proposed the motion and received the 350 thrones to carry on building The Towerjacks.

Fog on the brine.d: On the last night of the half-moon before the Equinox, a pearlescent, phosphorescent mist rose six or seven feet above the sea along the coasts of Feroz, Madruga, Sarvos, Necropolis, Redoubt and Spiral. It covers the northern half of the Bay, beginning a little over a dozen miles south of Feroz, follows only salt water, chokes the mouths of the four great rivers and resists sun and wind. It troubles fisherfolk and small boats and hides reefs and rocks, causing upsets for foreign ships, though Imperial traders who know the waters pass through. Detect magic reveals only a 30th magnitude Night effect that conceals information, including about itself. Magicians suggest The Eye of the High Places could examine it.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a Freeborn merchant grumbles that the fog might be some magician's work to protect against the Grendel, and their coast at Spiral is among those affected.
n.Highguard: Highguard's coastline at Necropolis was shrouded by the fog, adding to the hazards for its fisherfolk and small craft.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn coasts of Feroz and Madruga were engulfed; some greeted the fog with impromptu night-time parties and boat trips, though their fisherfolk soon found it gloomy and dangerous.
n.The League: Sarvos's shores were blanketed, prompting revelry among some boat owners at first, before the persistent fog began to hamper fishing and cause accidents.
n.Urizen: The Urizeni coast at Redoubt was among those where the fog appeared, bringing the same hazards to small boats and fishing.

t.Bay of Catazar: The whole northern half of the Bay lies beneath an impenetrable magical fog that conceals reefs and rocks, troubles small boats and foreign ships, yet leaves night skies unusually clear for star navigation.
t.Feroz: The fog rose along Feroz's coast and was found to begin a little over a dozen miles south of its tip; revellers took boats out to explore it on the first night.
t.Madruga: Madruga's coast was cloaked in the fog, which locals initially suspected was more magicians' meddling with the sky like that already seen in the territory.
t.Necropolis: The fog settled along Necropolis's coastline, lapping occasionally onto the shore but never spreading inland.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's shores were covered by the fog, making the waters hazardous for fishing boats and smaller vessels.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos saw impromptu parties and boat trips into the glowing fog on the first night, followed by growing concern as it lingered, hindered fisherfolk and caused accidents.
t.Spiral: The fog appeared along Spiral's coast at the same moment as elsewhere around the Bay, shrouding its waters.

Forge of sorrows.d: The Thule had dug tunnels beneath Gildenheim during their occupation and collapsed them when Imperial armies drove them out, apparently to hide the runeforge and perhaps return for it later. Some speculated the whole invasion of Skarsind aimed at acquiring it. The remains of Ryv Ironbones, a Navarri rune worker thought enslaved after the fall of Treji, were found there. Repair could be commissioned by the Senate for 60 wains of weirwood, 50 of mithril, 40 of white granite and at least 50 Thrones, taking six months and creating a new title. The Senate did not commission it; the opportunity remains, but as Skarsind now belongs to the Imperial Orcs, any national runeforge there would go to the Orcs.

n.Imperial Orcs: With Skarsind now theirs, any rebuilt runeforge there established as a national resource would belong to the Imperial Orcs rather than Wintermark.
n.Navarr: The skeleton of Ryv Ironbones, a Navarri rune worker believed enslaved by the Thule after the fall of Treji, was found in the ruins, suggesting he had been forced to work on the forge.
n.Thule: The Thule had secretly tunnelled to the runeforge, used slave labour to try to repair it and collapsed the passages on retreat, possibly intending to return; some speculated their invasion of Skarsind sought this prize.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk explorers and architects found and assessed the runeforge, but the pending relinquishment of Skarsind meant Wintermark would not gain it as a national resource.

t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Treji in Hercynia is cited as when Ryv Ironbones was believed taken into Thule slavery.
t.Skarsind: Deep beneath the cave of ice at Gildenheim lies an ancient runeforge that could be repaired in six months if commissioned, now within Imperial Orc territory.

Good faith.d: After negotiations collapsed and the Grendel assaulted The Fist, copies of a letter from High Lady Suriad, Salt Lord of Dubhtraig and Head of the Council of Attar, reached Navarr couriers and were passed on to senators and notable citizens. She accused the Empire of piracy on the Bay of Catazar and of twice negotiating in bad faith, and declared that the hostages would work the salt. Those who know the Grendel say this means a short, brutal life of slavery in their salt mines, and that once the captives reach Attar any hope of recovering them is lost. In response, the Senate voted to invite a Grendel delegation to Anvil at the Winter Solstice to discuss terms for ending the war.

n.Grendel: The Grendel, led by High Lady Suriad, abandoned any pretence of seeking peace and refused to free the Imperial hostages, an act that shows how furious, and perhaps surprised, they were at how their negotiations with the Empire had gone.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Navarr couriers received copies of the Grendel letter and delivered them to senators and other notable citizens.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel blamed Imperial 'merchants' for decades of piracy on the Bay of Catazar, claiming they wanted no war there while declaring that the Empire's demands for war would now be met.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is not named, though the letter refers to an earlier Grendel offer to restore land to the Empire in exchange for an end to piracy.

Hearth Tithe.d: The invasion of Lasambria ended the ceasefire with the Jotun before the Spring Equinox 380YE, when the western Empire was poorly prepared. Tassato's fortifications were only just complete, Overton was still being built, most Marcher armies were in the east, and Wintermark was weakened by curses. Community spirit rose in response, and talk turned to the Hearth Tithe. Dating from Emperor James's time, it saw farmers grow medicinal herbs for physicks, apothecaries and grimnir. A national assembly could revive it with a judgement, virtuous auras, a named priest and liao. At the Autumn Equinox, Wintermark named Ealstan of Stormspire and the Marches named James Appleseeder of Upwold. The Hearth Tithe would run in both nations for a year.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: one story claims the Hearth Tithe came from pre-Marcher Dawn, perhaps growing out of noble houses forcing yeomen to grow herbs instead of food.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: in the story, a Marcher farmer takes comfort that the Druj have fled back east, and the Abbott notes the fighting in Reikos.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Abbott in the story refers to the war with the Grendel in the south.
n.Jotun: The early end of the ceasefire after the invasion of Lasambria left the western Empire facing imminent Jotun invasion. That threat prompted the revival of the Hearth Tithe.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the fortifications at Tassato are noted as only just complete, and a Marcher recruit has gone to fight in Holberg.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly revived the Hearth Tithe and named James Appleseeder of Upwold to lead it. For a year, Marcher farms would give up some produce to grow cerulean mazzarine, marrowort and true vervain for the war effort.
n.Wintermark: Weakened by curses but rallying, Wintermark revived the Hearth Tithe through its assembly, with Ealstan of Stormspire named to encourage it. Its farms would grow healing herbs for a year, traditionally given to the grimnir who march with Winterfolk armies.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: one story holds that Marcher grain merchants first saw the Hearth Tithe in Hahnmark during old border hostilities between Wintermark and the Marches.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: in the story, a Marcher farmer's granddaughter has gone to Holberg to fight with Old Tom's brigade under Dick Talbot.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold is not named on the page, though the expected Jotun invasion of the western Empire forms the backdrop.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Abbott notes that the Bounders and Strong Reeds are in Reikos helping the Highborn reclaim their homes, and that sickness has taken many there.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the fortifications at Tassato are described as only just complete when the ceasefire ended.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: James Appleseeder of Upwold was the priest the Marcher assembly named to coordinate the Hearth Tithe.

Professional killers.d: A fortnight after the Summer Solstice, Edgar of Woldstone was attacked while researching the vallorn's origins in Rundhal. Marcher yeomen Warren of Aldstock and Jennifer Greenwood drove off the masked assassin, who died fleeing. Kallavesi mystics helped confirm it was a faceless herald, whose remains dissolved; its mask and gloves later vanished in transit to the Castle of Thorns. A second attacker escaped into a canal, and a third was captured in Helena Raminci di Sarvos's library. Found guilty of murder by Magistrate Avedon de Remourics, the herald destroyed itself. The Conclave later placed the Whisper Gallery under enmity. The Senate kept funding protection, but only two historical research projects could still be commissioned each season.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the herald's mask and gloves vanished from a sealed box while being sent to the Castle of Thorns in Astolat.
n.Wintermark: Several Kallavesi mystics helped Edgar of Woldstone examine the dead assassin, confirming it was a faceless herald rather than a mortal.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the herald's mask and gloves were being taken to the Castle of Thorns in Astolat when they disappeared in transit.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the mystics who helped identify the slain herald are described as Kallavesi, though the examination took place in Rundhal.

Provide aid to the Hierro Clan.d: Proposed by Feroz and seconded by the senator for Segura, the motion directed the civil service to supply the Hierro Clan, refugees then camped in Segura, with vital provisions. It was passed with an ongoing cost of 75 thrones each season. As a result, the Hierro Clan began receiving supplies and had not, at the time, been forced to turn to banditry to survive.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's senators drove the motion that saw the Empire take on the cost of feeding the Hierro Clan refugees sheltering in their nation, keeping them from turning to banditry.

t.Segura: The Hierro Clan refugees camped in Segura began receiving Imperial supplies, which had so far kept them from resorting to banditry in the territory.

Raise Varushkan army.d: The motion let the Varushkans begin raising a new army in Karsk. It cost 160 wains of mithril and 40 thrones, needed a year to raise and carried an upkeep of 50 thrones per season. No progress could be made until work began to rebuild the roads of Karsk, and that work had to be finished before the army could be completed. The motion arose from an opportunity concerning Varushkan forces already in Karsk, especially the people of Branoc and Moresvah. The materials were supplied over the following year: Maximov Goraniv Strascovich provided 80 wains of mithril, and Maarit Akkova Cendro provided 80 wains and the 40 thrones by Autumn 380YE.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained the right to raise a new Imperial army, the Iron Helms, and Varushkan citizens went on to supply all of the mithril and thrones it needed.

t.Karsk: Karsk, then uncontrolled, was chosen as the mustering ground for the Iron Helms, but the army depended on first rebuilding the territory's roads.

r.Karsk/Branoc: The people of Branoc were named in the opportunity behind the motion, which concerned Varushkan forces already present in Karsk.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The inhabitants of Moresvah were named alongside Branoc in the opportunity that led to raising a Varushkan army in Karsk.

Reap what you sow.d: Troubled by their Prosperity and by word from Anvil that Wintermark had sold them out, the people of Skarsind did not resent the Imperial Orcs. They still believed they deserved the fruits of their labour before handing over the land. Miners over-exploited the mines, leaving unsafe tunnels that would need a serious clean-up, possibly a Senate commission with weirwood-and-mithril supports. Foresters, herb gardeners and mana producers considered following suit. The Wintermark assembly passed two judgements and the Assembly of Loyalty one, all calling the practice unvirtuous. Over-production declined, but the remaining hard-liners' morale fell further. Meanwhile the curse on the Kallavesa marshes persisted unchanged.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard is not named on the page and is linked only through its holding of Casinea.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind was expected to become the Imperial Orcs' homeland. The Winterfolk there held no grudge and credited the orcs with helping liberate it, but they rushed to strip its wealth before handing it over.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Winterfolk of Skarsind are described as having struggled under Thule tyranny before liberation.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: recent events in Urizen are cited as one reason crystal mana was in demand.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's people in Skarsind felt betrayed by the rest of the nation. Its National Assembly passed two judgements condemning the strip-mining as unvirtuous, which reduced it but further lowered the hard-liners' morale.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea is not named on the page and is only associated with it on the map.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the auras spread to commemorate the Miracle at Hahnmark are noted as having faded.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa's marshes remained under a potent curse, with the draining of mana flows neither worsening nor improving.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind's miners over-exploited the mines, leaving unsafe tunnels, and other producers there considered over-harvesting too. Condemnation by the assemblies slowed the practice but deepened the gloom of those who persisted.

r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: Mystics reported eerie dancing lights over the Kallavesa Marsh and muttered grimly about what they might portend, as the curse on its mana continued.

Rebuild the roads of Karsk.d: Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by Holberg, the self-funded motion commissioned the Rebuilding of the Roads of Karsk at a cost of 80 wains of white granite and 20 thrones in labour, taking six months to construct. Radomir of Varushka supplied 40 wains of white granite and the 20 thrones after the Autumn Equinox 379YE, and the remaining 40 wains after the Winter Solstice 379YE. Once completed, the work will increase production for all mines and forests in Karsk, and restoring the roads to their former state will allow Varushka to support a third army.

n.Varushka: Varushka gains the prospect of supporting a third army once Karsk's roads are restored, with Radomir of Varushka supplying all the granite and thrones needed to build them.

t.Karsk: Karsk's devastated road network is to be rebuilt, and once completed the work will increase production for all mines and forests in the territory.

Red phoenix down.d: After the Spring Equinox, a thin, unnaturally penetrating drizzle soaked Redoubt, Zenith and Morrow at once. Urizen's many magicians grew lethargic, restless or short-tempered, struggling to keep their poise, with headaches and sleepless nights widespread. Mana sites in all three territories yielded half their normal crystal mana. The magicians quickly recognised the curse, though not who had cast it. Several weak regio collapsed and magical creatures grew more aggressive, with the trogoni driven into a ravenous frenzy that threatened mines, especially tempest jade mines. Coming after a similar situation in the League, mana shortages led the Imperial Bourse to offer no crystal mana at the coming Equinox auctions. The curse later abated and conditions returned to normal.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are not named; the only link is a comparison with the torrential rain of Reikos, and the page does not say who cast the curse.
n.Urizen: Urizen's magicians, a large share of its people, struggled to keep their poise under the curse, and the nation lost half its crystal mana, saw weak regio collapse and faced frenzied trogoni threatening its mines.

t.Morrow: Morrow was one of the three cursed territories, enduring the cold, seeping rain and halved production at its mana sites until the curse lifted.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt suffered the curse's drizzle and malaise, and its mana sites produced only half their usual crystal mana.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the curse's thin drizzle is contrasted with the torrential rain of Reikos.
t.Zenith: Zenith fell under the curse alongside Morrow and Redoubt, with sodden libraries and stores, troubled magicians and mana sites yielding only half their output.

Reed of fortune.d: Although Ephisis lacked amity, Reed, a powerful genie, was seen across the Empire over three months. He spoke with League silversmiths and printers, a Feroz paradour mistress, Atalyan shipwrights, the Imperial Mint, Bourse auctioneers, Wintermark smiths, Marcher merchants and others about their work and their politics. This raised suspicion that an Imperial citizen had summoned him by ritual. At Anvil he offered to purchase amity for no more than one hour so that the City of Gold and Lead could make a single address. He suggested a Declaration of Neutrality be raised alongside it, scrupulously following protocol. The Conclave declared amity, heard his address, and then restored neutrality.

n.The Brass Coast: Reed took syrah with the mistress of a Feroz paradour and counted planks on the docks of the Atalyan shipyard as part of his audit of Freeborn commerce.
n.The League: League craftsmen drew Reed's attention: he talked business with silversmiths in Temeschwar and printers in Tassato, and was reportedly seen outside a theatre in Sarvos.
n.The Marches: Reed evaluated the price of grain, beets and beer with Marcher merchants and was reported in Bregasland. The tale's opening tells of a genie who counted a Marcher farm's grain and helped dig a ditch by borrowing a farmhand's time.
n.Wintermark: Reed watched a Wintermark forge from sunrise to sunset while barely speaking to the hard-working smiths.

t.Bregasland: Somewhat unreliable reports placed Reed in Bregasland, deep in conversation with a Winter Sun orc.
t.Feroz: In Feroz the herald took syrah with the mistress of a paradour, questioning her about her trade.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the page does not name Madruga; its only Brass Coast references are a Feroz paradour and the Atalyan shipyard.
t.Sarvos: Scattered, unreliable reports placed Reed outside a theatre in Sarvos one night.
t.Tassato: Reed was spotted discussing business with printers in Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Reed was spotted discussing business with silversmiths in Temeschwar.

Rise of the Fellowship of Purple Sails.d: The Senate had reinstated civil servant observers on all Imperial fleets, which ended piracy against foreign nations and trade with the Jotun and Grendel. The Fellowship credits the observers with Imperial ships being welcomed without suspicion in some foreign ports. It gave fifty Thrones and promised fifty more each season while the policy stands, which in effect covers its cost. It hinted at longer-term plans, with enquiries directed to Michael of Crown's Quay. Rigia's green iron offering grew, but Jarm's House of Princes banned selling mana crystals to Imperial citizens. Sumaah closed Zemeh to Imperial citizens and expelled traders and diplomats. The Commonwealth kept up tariffs and red tape.

n.Grendel: While the civil servants remain aboard, Imperial fleets cannot be used to trade with Grendel forces.
n.Highguard: Highborn benefactors and priests of Prosperity back the Fellowship, praising enforcement of the law abroad as a source of Prosperity and Pride. The Highborn Michael of Crown's Quay is its point of contact.
n.Jotun: Imperial fleets can no longer trade with the Jotun while the observers stay aboard. In the story, would-be pirates are told they could give up their ships and go and fight the Jotun instead.
n.The League: League merchants and ship-captains are a core part of the Fellowship, which they joined after profiting from the warmer welcome Imperial ships now receive. One League captain complains of losing profit to Jarm's new ban on selling mana.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: captains troubled by Commonwealth tariffs are advised to speak to Senator Atte of Sermersuaq.

t.Necropolis: Anyone interested in the Fellowship's long-term plans can send a Winged Messenger to Michael of Crown's Quay in Necropolis. The unfinished Sumaah embassy is also being built in Necropolis.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Senator Atte of Sermersuaq is named as the person captains should approach about the Commonwealth's trade difficulties.

Rose of Astolat.d: The Castle of Thorns, once seat of the Dawnish monarchs and now a Civil Service academy housing apartments for Dawnish senators, began to fail: part of the eastern rampart collapsed, the buttresses of the Hall of Ten Nations cracked, giant rats infested the cellars and the roses died, which many took as an omen of rot at the Empire's heart. Paperwork went astray, staff grew absent-minded, ill and quarrelsome. Divination revealed a Winter curse, and maintenance costs rose, known only to the Auditor of the Imperial Treasury, Gerard La Salle, with a risk of decommissioning. An Urizen coven's ritual, which had unexpected side effects, and Dawnish action restored the castle.

n.Dawn: A great symbol of Dawnish glory and the apartments of its senators were threatened with ruin, and the people of Dawn took several steps to address the wound to their national pride before the castle was restored.
n.Urizen: A powerful Urizen coven performed a ritual at the Autumn Equinox to reinforce and repair the Castle of Thorns, which had unexpected side effects and helped bring about its restoration.

t.Astolat: The Castle of Thorns in Astolat suffered collapsing ramparts, dying roses, rat infestation and a curse on its occupants until it was restored to full strength and the Winter malaise departed.

Sitskrieg.d: After seasons of raiding, the Jotun were met by Imperial fortifications and armies, including those of the Freeborn, the Mark, Dawn and the Imperial Orcs, as well as personal retinues sent by several nations, and were driven back across the border. Only scattered reports came in: a large warband moving south past Rest in Kallavesa, a heavy raid on five properties at Fisher's Rock in the North Fens, and three Jotun scouts at the Gilded Peak in Kahraman. The Winter Sun reported no raiders in the Grey Fens, and knights of the Hounds of Glory slaughtered raiders attacking stoneworks in Tassato. Some hailed the quiet as a triumph, but the raiders had been recalled by their Kings ahead of an imminent Jotun invasion.

n.Dawn: Dawn's army was among the Imperial forces positioned to defend the Western Empire against the Jotun raiders, whose withdrawal heralded a coming invasion.
n.Imperial Orcs: An Imperial Orc army was among the forces deployed against the Jotun raids, which have now given way to the threat of a full invasion.
n.Jotun: The Jotun Kings recalled their clan warriors from raiding the Empire, ending the raids as they prepared to invade.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven appears on the scribe's map as one of the territories she studied for signs of Jotun activity.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn armies helped hold the line against the raiders, and the only sign of the Jotun in Brass Coast lands was three scouts sighted at the Gilded Peak in Kahraman.
n.The League: Raiders who tried to attack the stoneworks under way in Tassato were slaughtered by knights of the Hounds of Glory, one of the last clashes before the raids fell silent.
n.The Marches: Armies of the Mark helped repel the raiders, but a heavy raid struck five properties at Fisher's Rock in Bregasland's North Fens, and the Marches lay in the path of the expected invasion.
n.Wintermark: A large warband was reported moving south past Rest in Kallavesa, one of the few signs of Jotun movement as Wintermark faced the prospect of invasion.

t.Bregasland: Bregasland suffered a heavy raid on five properties at Fisher's Rock in the North Fens, while the Winter Sun reported the Grey Fens free of raiders for a week.
t.Kahraman: Three Jotun scouts were sighted at the Gilded Peak in Kahraman, a lone sign of Jotun interest in the territory.
t.Kallavesa: Two reports placed a large Jotun warband moving south past Rest in Kallavesa.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is one of the territories the scribe scanned on her map while trying to predict Jotun movements.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq is one of the territories the scribe scanned on her map while trying to predict Jotun movements.
t.Tassato: Raiders attacking the stoneworks under construction in Tassato were cut down by knights of the Hounds of Glory.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold is one of the territories the scribe scanned on her map while trying to predict Jotun movements.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Winter Sun reported that no raiders had been seen in the Grey Fens for a week, a silence that foreshadowed the Jotun invasion.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: Five properties at Fisher's Rock in the North Fens were struck by a heavy Jotun raid.

Strange harvest.d: Ettercaps attacking settlements near the forest's edge were destroyed within three weeks by soldiers of the Northern Eagle and the Silent Sentinel in Casinea, the Castle of Thorns garrison in Astolat, and knights, yeofolk militia, troops from the Gate and Navarri thorns in Semmerholm. A transformation then struck farms and forests, cutting their output by a quarter. Vates confirmed the energy flowed from the Brocéliande vallorn along the trods, though the trods were undamaged. The seed pods risked breaching the Conclave's interdiction on vallorn seeds, and the Senate was invited to clarify the law. Cultivating the plant was possible with Spring magic. The vallorn later returned to quiescence, and nobody publicly admitted cultivating the fruit.

n.Dawn: Farms and forests in Astolat and Semmerholm lost a quarter of their produce, while Dawnish knights, yeofolk militia and the Castle of Thorns garrison fought off the ettercaps.
n.Highguard: Highborn farms and forests in Casinea lost a quarter of their output to the Spring transformation, and workers in Mareholm unearthed corrupted dragonbone.
n.Navarr: The Brocéliande vallorn was confirmed as the source of the transformation, carried along the trods; Navarri vates helped trace it and thorns from Boar's Dell fought in Semmerholm.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: troops from the Gate, the fortification guarding the passes into Holberg, helped defend Semmerholm.

t.Astolat: The Castle of Thorns garrison destroyed attacking ettercaps, but farms and forests lost a quarter of their produce, and beggarwood near Rucastle put forth foul blossoms that drew biting flies.
t.Brocéliande: The vallorn here unleashed miasma, ettercaps and a surge of Spring energy that flowed out along the trods before receding back into quiescence.
t.Casinea: Soldiers of the Northern Eagle and the Silent Sentinel kept the ettercaps within half a mile of the forest, but a quarter of the territory's farm and forest produce was twisted.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Gate guarding the now-secure passes into Holberg supplied seasoned troops to fight in Semmerholm.
t.Semmerholm: Questing knights, yeofolk militia, troops from the Gate and Navarri thorns put down the ettercap raids, but farms and forests lost a quarter of their produce to the transformation.

r.Brocéliande/Boar's Dell: Mentioned in passing: bands of Navarri thorns from Boar's Dell helped fight the ettercaps in Semmerholm.
r.Casinea/Mareholm: Highborn workers in Mareholm unearthed half-formed, corrupted deposits of dragonbone twisted into unsettling organic shapes.

The dead tree gives no shelter.d: Early rumours spoke of a Jotun invasion of fifteen thousand. Freeborn reports soon showed that the force was the remnant of the Hierro army: warriors and raiders escorting children and elderly orcs, with more arriving daily from Reinos and Kalino. They met no Imperial armies, but local Segurans took up arms, remembering the invasion of 363YE. The orcs had supplies only until about a week after the Equinox, after which they would have to scavenge or turn to banditry. The Senate or Synod could fund supplies, citizens could resupply them, and the Synod could send missionaries. The General Assembly appointed the Navarr priest Taryn of Exile's End to bring the Way to the orcs, funded with 100 liao.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Hierro showed no interest in joining the Imperial Orcs. Segurans who spoke with them found them ambivalent, and sometimes openly hostile, towards the orcs already in the Empire.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: early garbled reports wrongly claimed the orcs were the vanguard of a Jotun invasion, and they had crossed from Jotun-held Reinos.
n.Navarr: The Navarr priest Taryn of Exile's End was appointed by the Synod's General Assembly to lead efforts to bring the Way to the Lasambrian orcs.
n.The Brass Coast: Thousands of armed Lasambrian orcs camped in Freeborn Segura and would soon run out of food. Local Freeborn took up arms, recalling the 363YE invasion and generations of Hierro raids on their caravans.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: news of the orc incursion reached Sarvos and Tassato soon after the Brass Coast.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the nearest Imperial armies to the Hierro were in Feroz.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the nearest Imperial fortification to the orc camp was in Kahraman.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: more Hierro orcs arrived in Segura every day from Kalino as well as Reinos.
t.Reinos: The Hierro army and its baggage train crossed the border from Reinos into Segura, and more orcs continued to arrive from there daily.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: news of the orc crossing reached Sarvos early, soon after the Brass Coast.
t.Segura: Several thousand Lasambrian orcs camped in Segura with dwindling supplies. Armed Freeborn locals left a volatile situation that risked turning into banditry or open conflict.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: news of the orc crossing reached Tassato early, soon after the Brass Coast.

r.Segura/Anduzjasse: The Hierro crossed into Anduzjasse and set up a fortified makeshift camp twenty miles south-east of the partially rebuilt town of Anduz. They faced food shortages on its dry southern plains.
